applicable_when: The kernel runs on an H200 SXM5 with peak FP32 Tensor Core (TF32) throughput of 989 TFLOPS vs 67 TFLOPS for scalar FP32 FFMA — a ~14.7x hardware advantage. Currently ALLOW_TF32 = False is hardcoded, forcing tl.dot to use scalar FFMA and completely bypassing Tensor Cores. This explains the dismal 7.93% Compute SOL. Enabling allow_tf32=True in tl.dot will route the 32×32 matrix multiply through the H200's Tensor Core units. K=960 is large, so TF32 mantissa truncation (23→10 bits) may introduce small numerical error, but the diversity instruction explicitly targets this strategy.

strategy_title: Manual Tile Resize Without Autotune Causes Regression
strategy_description: Manually changing BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N from 32 to 64 and BLOCK_K from 128 to 32 without autotuning caused a 1.87x slowdown despite reducing shared memory bank conflicts (12-way conflicts persisted) and improving IPC. The instruction count exploded from 3.5M to 11.5M (3.26x increase) because the smaller BLOCK_K means more K-loop iterations, and register pressure increased from 94 to 128 registers/thread (hitting the 128 register cap), while achieved occupancy remained stuck at 6.25% — the same as before. The net effect was far more total work with no occupancy benefit, causing the kernel to run nearly 2x longer.
slow_pseudocode:
# Before: BLOCK_M=32, BLOCK_N=32, BLOCK_K=128
# grid = (80, 1, 1)
BLOCK_M : tl.constexpr = 32
BLOCK_N : tl.constexpr = 32
BLOCK_K : tl.constexpr = 128
# K-loop iterates K/BLOCK_K = 960/128 = 7.5 times
# Executed instructions: 3.5M, registers: 94/thread
fast_pseudocode:
# After (regressed): BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32
# grid = (80, 1, 1) — unchanged!
BLOCK_M : tl.constexpr = 64
BLOCK_N : tl.constexpr = 64
BLOCK_K : tl.constexpr = 32
# K-loop iterates K/BLOCK_K = 960/32 = 30 times
# Executed instructions: 11.5M, registers: 128/thread (capped)
# Grid unchanged — no occupancy improvement
applicable_when: Never apply this pattern. Manual tile size changes without updating the grid and without autotuning are an anti-pattern.
do_not_apply_when: Always avoid manually hardcoding new tile sizes without: (1) updating the launch grid to match new tile dimensions, (2) verifying register pressure does not increase to the hardware cap (128 regs/thread on H100/H200), (3) using @triton.autotune to search the configuration space. When BLOCK_K is reduced, the K-loop iteration count increases proportionally, multiplying total instruction count — this dominates if occupancy does not improve.
framework_notes: In Triton, reducing BLOCK_K from 128 to 32 increases K-loop iterations by 4x (960/32=30 vs 960/128=7.5), causing instruction count to multiply. Simultaneously, larger BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N tiles increase register usage per thread. If the grid size is not updated to reflect the new tile dimensions (e.g., grid should be (cdiv(M,BLOCK_M)*cdiv(N,BLOCK_N), 1, 1) not a fixed (80,1,1)), the number of output tiles computed per block increases, further multiplying work. The plan called for @triton.autotune but the implementation only changed constexpr values — the autotune decorator was never added, and the grid was not updated.
